questions.q: What is Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Solution, according to this lesson?
options: The real, widely-adopted, free, open-source community standard for SQL Server index/statistics maintenance and integrity checks, that almost nobody reinvents from scratch
A Microsoft-built feature that ships automatically inside every SQL Server installation
A paid, proprietary third-party monitoring tool
A deprecated tool no longer used in practice
questions.explain: Knowing this widely-used standard exists — and that recreating it is usually wasted effort — is itself real, practical DBA knowledge.

questions.q: Why should DBCC CHECKDB run before index maintenance, per this lesson's sequencing?
options: There's no point optimizing indexes on a database that might already be corrupted
DBCC CHECKDB has no relationship to index maintenance timing
Index maintenance must always run before any integrity check
The order maintenance jobs run in never actually matters
questions.explain: Running an integrity check first ensures you're not spending effort optimizing indexes on data that may already have a deeper problem.

questions.q: Why does statistics maintenance run AFTER index maintenance in the recommended sequence?
options: Rebuilding an index updates its statistics as a side effect, so a separate statistics pass afterward catches only what index maintenance didn't already touch
Statistics maintenance must always run completely independently, with no relationship to index maintenance
There is no real reason for this ordering
Index maintenance actually deletes all existing statistics
questions.explain: This ordering avoids redundant work by relying on the side effect index rebuilds already provide.

questions.q: How does a DBA's job around maintenance differ between Managed Instance/VM-hosted SQL Server and Azure SQL Database?
options: Managed Instance/VM requires the DBA to own the maintenance schedule directly; Azure SQL Database already automates much of it, shifting the DBA's job toward verifying that automation works
There is no meaningful difference between the two platforms for maintenance
Azure SQL Database requires MORE manual maintenance scheduling than Managed Instance
Managed Instance does not support any maintenance automation at all
questions.explain: This ties directly to Lesson 59's real platform difference in native Agent support.

questions.q: What real, practical DBA skill does knowing about Ola Hallengren's solution represent, beyond just using the tool?
options: Recognizing that recreating well-tested community tooling yourself is usually wasted effort, while still understanding Lesson 53's REBUILD/REORGANIZE trade-off to configure it sensibly
It replaces the need to understand REBUILD vs. REORGANIZE entirely
It means a DBA never needs to think about fragmentation again
It has no practical value beyond knowing the tool's name
questions.explain: Using a mature community tool doesn't replace the underlying understanding — you still need it to configure the tool's thresholds sensibly.
